source: Patel, Arocha, Groen (1987) Domain specificity and knowledge utilization in diagnostic explanation
finding: Defines the paradigm. Forward reasoning is a directed path from a finding to a hypothesis in a semantic network. Backward reasoning is a path from a hypothesis to a finding. Physicians explain a case of acute bacterial endocarditis; the diagnosis is asked for only after the explanation.
numbers: 6 cardiologists, 6 psychiatrists, 6 surgeons; one case with 5 components (infection, aortic insufficiency, embolic phenomena, acuteness, IV drug use).
quote: Forward reasoning corresponds to an oriented path from a fact to a hypothesis. Backward reasoning corresponds to a directed path from a hypothesis to a fact.
limits: Small N. Hand-coded semantic networks. Only one case. Direction labels depend on the coder.
agent_relevance: Our agent can log each step as finding-to-hypothesis or hypothesis-to-finding; a cheap trace label.

source: Patel, Arocha, Groen (1987) specialty focus results
finding: Each specialty explained the component close to its own domain. Cardiologists explained aortic insufficiency; psychiatrists explained drug use; surgeons explained infection. Specialty knowledge decides which parts of a case get explained.
numbers: Subjects (of 6) explaining each component: cardiologists drug use 2, infection 4, acuteness 1, aortic insufficiency 6, emboli 5. Psychiatrists 5, 5, 2, 2, 2. Surgeons 6, 6, 5, 2, 3.
limits: Counts only, no inferential tests. Measures focus, not diagnostic accuracy.
agent_relevance: Anchoring on the familiar part of a case is expected. A scaffold step could force the agent to list every case component and who explains it.

source: Patel, Arocha, Groen (1987) directionality conclusion
finding: A mixture of forward and backward reasoning appears in every protocol. More forward-directed reasoning is used in a familiar situation; more backward in an unfamiliar one. Some protocols alternate forward and backward in chains.
numbers: Cardiologist 7: components 1 and 2 mixed, component 3 pure forward. Psychiatrist 2: no component pure forward or pure backward.
quote: A more forward directed reasoning strategy is used in a familiar situation and a more backward reasoning strategy is used in an unfamiliar situation.
limits: Qualitative; exemplar protocols with network figures, no group statistics on proportion forward.
agent_relevance: Pure direction is the exception. Do not design the agent as one direction only.

source: Patel, Arocha, Groen (1987) review of earlier work (Joseph and Patel 1986; Patel, Arocha, Groen 1986)
finding: Experts reach the diagnosis early and read later findings as support; subexperts (physicians outside their specialty) keep generating new hypotheses. Cardiologists given an endocrine (hypothyroidism) case read some findings as cardiac, more so on hard cases. Forward reasoning is proposed as the verbal-domain counterpart of perceptual pattern recognition (radiology, Lesgold et al.).
numbers: No new numbers; secondhand description.
limits: Secondhand. The same paper says easy and typical cases in own specialty give forward reasoning, hard or out-of-specialty cases give backward.
agent_relevance: Early lock-in plus confirmation is what guardrails against premature closure target.

source: Arocha and Patel (1991) Hypothesis generation and the coordination of theory and evidence in medical diagnostic reasoning
finding: Medical students and one resident diagnosed two cardiology cases shown in 3 segments with think-aloud. All used a mix of forward and backward reasoning, but more forward-directed reasoning went with diagnostic accuracy. Year-2 students kept their first hypothesis against contrary evidence; later students held concurrent hypotheses.
numbers: McGill; 4 students per year group (years 2, 3, 4) plus 1 cardiology resident; 90 minute session; 2 cases. Correct diagnosis in 5 subjects: two year-2, two year-4, the resident; no year-3 student; only the resident correct on both cases.
quote: A more forward-directed reasoning was related to diagnostic accuracy.
limits: N = 13. Accuracy link not tested statistically. Cases built to suggest a wrong first hypothesis.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis-first work by weak knowers locks onto the first idea. Our agent should re-check the first hypothesis against contradicting findings.

source: Arocha and Patel (1991) hypothesis counts and confirmation share
finding: Number of hypotheses rose with training. Confirmation was the main evaluation strategy in all groups. Year-2 students ignored or reinterpreted contradicting cues; the resident narrowed to one hypothesis that explained most data.
numbers: Mean hypotheses after segment 1: year 2 = 1.5, year 3 = 3, year 4 = 3.4, resident = 5 in both cases. Confirming relations: year 2 71 percent, years 3 and 4 88 percent, resident 92 percent of cues.
limits: Tiny groups. Confirmation is high in everyone, so it does not separate experts from novices.
agent_relevance: Confirmation dominates in all groups. A scaffold needs an explicit disconfirmation step, not only generate-and-confirm.

source: Arocha and Patel (1991) resident versus year-2 student on case VP45
finding: The resident listed many initial diagnoses (breadth-first), then used backward inference to reach the correct pericarditis, by postulating two mechanisms and matching the cue pattern. The year-2 student kept myocardial infarction and modified it.
numbers: Four subjects who were correct used forward inference for the final diagnosis, all on case 2. The resident used backward inference on case 1 after contradictory evidence.
limits: One-subject contrast. Authors say such backward use needs a vast biomedical background to succeed.
agent_relevance: Backward reasoning is not only a novice mode. Experts use it as a mechanism check when forward fails.

source: Arocha and Patel (1991) theoretical frame on direction
finding: Forward: evidence to hypothesis, fast, efficient when knowledge suffices. Backward: hypothesis generates evidence, slow, heavy on working memory, tied to unsuccessful novice performance, yet found in experts in some domains (Larkin et al.; Anderson on programming). Cites Patel, Groen and Norman (in press): problem-based-learning students used more backward reasoning and more elaboration, conventional-curriculum students more forward.
numbers: No new data.
limits: Curriculum finding is secondhand. It suggests direction is partly a training artefact rather than a pure expertise marker.
agent_relevance: Treat direction as a function of knowledge and training, not a fixed marker of ability.

source: Arocha and Patel (1991) summary of Joseph and Patel (1990): generation versus evaluation
finding: Generating hypotheses does not separate low- from high-knowledge physicians; evaluating them does. High-knowledge subjects searched for confirmation and refined their first hypothesis; low-knowledge subjects generated alternatives after they already had the correct one.
numbers: Endocrinology case; low knowledge = physicians without the specialty. N not given in this text.
limits: Secondhand report.
agent_relevance: Generation is cheap and shared; the scaffold's value sits in the evaluation step.

source: Coderre, Mandin, Harasym, Fick (2004) Impact of two multiple-choice question formats on the problem-solving strategies used by novices and experts
finding: Think-aloud on 4 presentations (liver enzymes, nausea and vomiting, diarrhea, dysphagia) with multiple-choice and extended-matching items. Experts used pattern recognition or scheme-inductive (forward) reasoning much more than novices. Hypothetico-deductive (backward, to-and-fro) was a fallback.
numbers: 20 experts (gastroenterologists), 20 non-experts; 80 coded items per format per group. Experts hypothetico-deductive 5 and 5, scheme 36 and 30, pattern recognition 39 and 45 (MCQ, EMQ). Non-experts HD 37 and 32, scheme 28 and 26, pattern 15 and 22. Expert vs non-expert coefficient for using an expert process 2.69 (CI 1.64 to 3.75), about threefold odds. Judge agreement 0.84.
quote: Deductive reasoning (hypothetico-deductive) is a 'to-and-fro' strategy of problem solving, also termed 'backward reasoning'.
limits: Strategy coded from think-aloud; rater judgement. Non-experts still used forward methods more than 50 percent of the time. Items are exam questions, not live cases.
agent_relevance: The expert-novice gap in direction is real but partial. Keep the weight modest in design.

source: Coderre et al. (2004) task difficulty as boundary condition
finding: Diarrhea items were the most complex for both groups, and both moved toward hypothetico-deductive reasoning there. For experts, nausea and vomiting with metabolic causes was also complex and pulled them to backward reasoning.
numbers: Diarrhea: experts HD 2 and 1 of 20 per format versus non-experts 13 and 14 of 20. Coefficient for hard presentations -1.55 (CI -2.67 to -0.43, p 0.01).
limits: Difficulty defined after the fact by the authors.
agent_relevance: Direction depends on the problem as well as the person. The agent should shift to hypothesis-driven checks when the case is unfamiliar.

source: Coderre et al. (2004) definition of the three strategies
finding: Three strategies: hypothetico-deductive (backward; novices or fallback), pattern recognition, and scheme-inductive reasoning (forward along a decision tree with crucial tests; used by experts when pattern recognition is not possible).
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Taxonomy of this group, not universal.
agent_relevance: Scheme-inductive reasoning is forward but structured like a checklist tree. It matches a fixed-schema scaffold.

source: Coderre, Mandin, Harasym, Fick (2003) Diagnostic reasoning strategies and diagnostic success, Medical Education
finding: Cited by Coderre 2004 as the source of the scheme-inductive idea and of the claim that experts use pattern recognition and scheme-inductive reasoning, which go with higher accuracy than hypothetico-deductive reasoning.
numbers: Numbers not verified; full text not opened.
limits: Recalled from the citing paper and a search listing; do not quote numbers until opened.
agent_relevance: Primary evidence that forward methods go with accuracy. Needs a proper read in a later angle.

source: Experienced physicians benefit from analyzing initial diagnostic hypotheses (2013), Canadian Medical Education Journal
finding: Nephrologists and residents gave an initial diagnosis, then were primed to analyse the rest with hypothetico-deductive or scheme-inductive reasoning. Analysis helped both groups. Residents did better with scheme-inductive reasoning; experienced nephrologists showed no difference between strategies.
numbers: 9 nephrologists, 6 residents, 10 cases. Initial accuracy 34.7 percent. Final: nephrologists 31.1 to 65.6 percent (p<0.001), residents 40.0 to 70.0 percent (p<0.001). 35 percent of diagnoses changed; 96 percent of changes wrong-to-right, 4 percent right-to-wrong. Residents scheme-inductive OR 5.69 (1.59 to 20.33); nephrologists OR 0.57 (0.23 to 1.39). Interaction p about 0.02.
limits: N = 15. The abstract and results give different p values for the resident OR (0.07 versus under 0.01); check. Not the Patel group.
agent_relevance: Forcing structured forward analysis helps weaker knowers, not experts. A scaffold gains most when the underlying model is weaker.

source: Experienced physicians benefit from analyzing initial diagnostic hypotheses (2013): change rates
finding: Likelihood of changing the initial diagnosis did not differ by experience or by strategy, so the strategy effect lies in the quality of change, not the amount.
numbers: Change rate by group p 0.70; by strategy p 0.90.
limits: Same small sample.
agent_relevance: Supports a 'second look at the first hypothesis' step with high gain per token.

source: Patel and Groen (1986) Knowledge based solution strategies in medical reasoning, Cognitive Science 10:91-116
finding: The founding paper. Expert cardiologists on the endocarditis case: accurate diagnosers fit pure forward reasoning through causal rules. Per the 1987 paper (opened), cardiologists who solved it more completely used the rules linking puncture wounds to IV drug use to infection and early diastolic murmur to aortic valve insufficiency.
numbers: Original numbers not verified: publisher PDF request returned an HTML page. Cited 632 times (Semantic Scholar).
limits: Not opened. Treat figures as unconfirmed.
agent_relevance: The paper that named the idea; background.

source: Patel, Groen, Arocha (1990) Medical expertise as a function of task difficulty, Memory and Cognition 18
finding: Cited by Arocha and Patel (1991) as showing that expert backward reasoning appears on hard cases. Needs a read for numbers.
numbers: Not verified.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Key boundary condition against the simple 'experts are forward' story.

source: Larkin, McDermott, Simon, Simon (1980) Expert and novice performance in solving physics problems, Science 208
finding: General source of the forward-expert, backward-novice contrast outside medicine; cited by the medical papers.
numbers: Not verified here.
limits: Mapping to medicine is by analogy. Not opened.
agent_relevance: Suggests the effect is a general knowledge effect.

source: Elstein, Shulman, Sprafka (1978) Medical problem solving, Harvard University Press
finding: The hypothetico-deductive account. Arocha and Patel (1991) say Groen and Patel (1985) challenged it as a description of what people do, arguing it is an intellectual tool, not a habit.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Known only through the 1991 summary.
agent_relevance: The competing model. Our scaffold uses hypothesis testing as a prescribed tool, which fits the 'intellectual tool' reading.

source: Dunbar and Schunn (1990); Klahr and Dunbar (1988), as described by Arocha and Patel (1991)
finding: Scientific discovery searches a hypothesis space and an experiment space. Subjects retrieve a hypothesis from a similar past case, test it, and if it fails seek another or adjust the current one to fit the data.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Secondhand.
agent_relevance: Maps onto generate-test-revise cycles in the scaffold.

source: Mapping clinical reasoning literature across the health professions: a scoping review (2020)
finding: Lists forward and backward reasoning among the reasoning processes studied, next to pattern recognition and hypothetico-deductive reasoning. The part I read gave no new test of the Patel-Groen claim.
numbers: Scoping review; counts not extracted.
limits: Only keyword terms were read, not the full synthesis.
agent_relevance: Confirms the distinction is a standard label.

source: Diagnosing virtual patients: the interplay between knowledge and diagnostic activities (2023)
finding: Diagnostic process activities (hypothesis generation, evidence generation, evidence evaluation) explain diagnostic success beyond knowledge.
numbers: N = 106 German medical students (years 3 to 5). Knowledge had a small association with accuracy; activities added unique variance in hierarchical regressions.
limits: Students, virtual patients. Does not measure forward versus backward direction.
agent_relevance: Process adds value even with knowledge fixed, which is what a scaffold assumes.

source: Transforming clinical reasoning: the role of AI in supporting human cognitive limitations (2025)
finding: Describes scheme-inductive reasoning as forward reasoning from symptoms to diagnoses through schemata, used when pattern recognition leaves uncertainty. Positions AI as support for human limits.
numbers: Review; no measured LLM result on forward versus backward found in the text read.
limits: Narrative review.
agent_relevance: The LLM literature cites the distinction conceptually, not experimentally.

source: LLM studies testing forward versus backward reasoning in diagnosis (search status)
finding: No direct LLM test of the Patel-Groen claim was found. arXiv returned zero hits on several queries (a weak negative), Europe PMC returned only reviews and generic LLM diagnosis studies, and OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were rate limited.
numbers: 0 relevant LLM studies in about 8 database queries.
limits: WebSearch budget ran out after one useful query; absence is not proven.
agent_relevance: Leave to the LLM angle; no LLM direction effect is established.
